subject.title: Feature Request: Add parseMode config for Telegram channels

question: Should OpenClaw add a public Telegram parse/text-mode config, and which modes, defaults, and per-account overrides should it support?
rationale: The missing source path is clear, but choosing between current HTML, plain/no-parse, MarkdownV2, rich-message interaction, raw HTML/custom emoji behavior, and account inheritance changes public config and Telegram rendering/security semantics.

options.title: Approve a narrow text-mode config
options.body: Add a typed Telegram-owned setting with conservative values such as current HTML plus plain/no-parse, keeping defaults unchanged and deferring raw HTML/custom emoji/MarkdownV2 expansion until separately approved.

options.title: Keep current knobs only
options.body: Decline parse-mode config for now and rely on `richMessages`, `markdown.tables`, and the standard HTML renderer, leaving this issue open only if a narrower rendering bug remains.

options.title: Design a broader rendering API
options.body: Treat parse mode as part of a larger channel formatting contract with message entities or plugin hooks, likely superseding this issue with a broader design item.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow text-mode config
recommendation.body: Add a typed Telegram-owned setting with conservative values such as current HTML plus plain/no-parse, keeping defaults unchanged and deferring raw HTML/custom emoji/MarkdownV2 expansion until separately approved.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already reviewed this issue's product boundary and has history on the Telegram HTML formatting behavior that the request is trying to make configurable.
